classification.difficultyReason: Model two journey times with algebraic denominators, form a quadratic and select the physically valid root.

content.prompt: A car travels 500 km at a constant speed. If it had travelled at a speed 10 km/h less, it would have taken 1 hour more to travel the distance. Find the speed of the car, correct to two decimal places.

answer.short:
$5(1+\sqrt{201})\text{ km/h}\approx75.89\text{ km/h}$.

Use time = distance ÷ speed to form a quadratic, then take the root greater than 10.
answer.worked:
Let the car's speed be $v$ km/h, where $v>10$. Using time = distance ÷ speed, the original time is $\frac{500}{v}$ hours and the slower journey takes $\frac{500}{v-10}$ hours.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{500}{v-10}&=\frac{500}{v}+1\\500v&=500(v-10)+v(v-10)\\500v&=500v-5000+v^2-10v\\v^2-10v-5000&=0.\end{align*}$$
Here $a=1$, $b=-10$ and $c=-5000$.
$$\begin{align*}b^2-4ac&=(-10)^2-4(1)(-5000)\\b^2-4ac&=20100.\end{align*}$$
The quadratic formula gives
$$\begin{align*}v&=\frac{10\pm\sqrt{20100}}{2}\\v&=5\pm5\sqrt{201}.\end{align*}$$
Reject $5-5\sqrt{201}$ because it is negative. Thus the car's speed is $5(1+\sqrt{201})\text{ km/h}\approx75.89\text{ km/h}$.

Check: for this positive root, $v(v-10)=5000$, so
$$\frac{500}{v-10}-\frac{500}{v}=\frac{5000}{v(v-10)}=1\text{ hour}.$$
